items.item_text: California Licensed Pharmacy Technician
Minimum education satisfied through attainment of the required licensure/certification
Two (2) years of recent experience as a licensed Pharmacy Technician in an outpatient pharmacy
One (1) year of recent experience routinely performing inventory management functions in an outpatient pharmacy
Experience performing medication supply and inventory management functions in a health-system Outpatient Pharmacy or Specialty Pharmacy
Experience using Epic Willow Ambulatory and Epic Willow Inventory to support pharmacy operations and medication supply workflows
Experience supporting 340B medication supply, distribution, or other pharmacy operations that contribute to cost savings and financial stewardship
Experience reviewing medication utilization, inventory, and supply reports to identify stock needs, trends, and areas requiring follow-up
Experience obtaining medications through wholesalers, manufacturers, and other pharmaceutical vendors
Experience using Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook, for routine reporting, documentation, and communication
Experience coordinating medication shipments, bulk product movement, returns, or inventory issue escalation across pharmacy locations

This Pharmacy Technician 3 serves as the centralized operational resource and escalation pathway between Specialty Pharmacy hub-based prescription-processing teams and Health Solutions Pharmacy (HSP) inventory and dispensing operations. The position supports multiple service lines who may not have direct visibility to pharmacy inventory. The position investigates and coordinates resolution of medication availability concerns, including inventory uncertainty, shortages, stock-outs, backorders, allocations, receiving issues, and unexpected changes in demand. Working with pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, inventory personnel, Pharmacy Supply Chain, and operational leaders, the position anticipates medication needs, communicates status and next steps, and escalates unresolved concerns before medication availability affects patient care. The role also supports financial stewardship, HSP inventory operations, returns, stock-out management, shipping of products in bulk, and the operational needs of HSP and 340B teams. #CA-DS
60% - Specialty Pharmacy and Hub Inventory Management, Mitigation, and Escalation
20% - Health Solutions Pharmacy Inventory Operations
20% - Shipping Coordination and Bulk Product Movement
Ability to independently manage medication availability, stock levels, and day-to-day supply needs in an outpatient or Specialty Pharmacy setting

Ability to effectively use Epic Willow Ambulatory, including inventory management functionality, to support medication supply and inventory workflows, review inventory information, and identify concerns requiring follow-up
Ability to troubleshoot medication supply concerns, coordinate appropriate follow-up, and escalate issues as needed to support resolution
Working knowledge of medication supply and inventory management practices within a health-system outpatient or Specialty Pharmacy setting
Ability to routinely review medication utilization, inventory, and supply reports and identify concerns requiring follow-up
Ability to assess medication utilization, inventory, and supply reports to identify changing medication needs, stock-level concerns, and opportunities for adjustment
Ability to address medication shortages, backorders, allocations, product availability, and other pharmaceutical supply-chain challenges
Knowledge of drug shortages, backorders, allocations, limited-distribution medications, and pharmaceutical supply-chain processes
Ability to use pharmacy information systems and computer applications to support daily medication supply and inventory workflows
Ability to anticipate medication supply needs based on utilization, patient demand, stock levels, product availability, and market conditions
Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with effective written and verbal communication and the ability to collaborate across teams
Knowledge of inventory management principles, including medication availability, days-on-hand, stock-outs, excess product, waste, and cost
Ability to effectively share medication supply knowledge and provide guidance and education to pharmacy staff and other team members
Ability to collaborate across pharmacy operations, Purchasing, Supply Chain, and other teams to address complex medication supply concerns
Knowledge of California pharmacy law, applicable regulatory requirements, pharmacy terminology, and generic and brand medication names
Knowledge of applicable medication supply and regulatory requirements, including DSCSA, recalls, and product tracing
Ability to recognize situations outside Pharmacy Technician scope or authority and appropriately refer or escalate concerns
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint, to support routine reporting, documentation, communication, and operational activities
Ability to function as a centralized escalation resource and coordinate closed-loop follow-up across remote prescription-processing teams and pharmacy-based inventory operations
